catholic-encyclopedia-1913-mostar-and-ma:
Mostar and Markana-Trebinje are dioceses in Herzegovina, formed when the Berlin Congress of 1878 let Austria-Hungary occupy Bosnia and Herzegovina. The religious settlement followed at once. In 1881 Emperor Francis Joseph created the church province of Sarajevo, with Banjaluka, Mostar and Markana-Trebinje as suffragans. The Bishop of Mostar administers Markana-Trebinje through a pro-vicar.

Mostar, capital of Herzegovina with 15,000 people including 3,500 Catholics, takes its region's name from the title Herzog, duke, given in 1448 to Grand Waywode Stephan Vukcic. Herzegovina fell to the Turks in 1483 after its last Bosnian king was beheaded in defiance of a promise. The entry traces its peoples, Orthodox, Muslim, Catholic and Jewish, the Eastern Schism, the Bogomil sect, and the church's modern recovery.

nasa-tm-19670013511-effect-of-simulated-:
Roy G. Stabe, John F. Kline, and Edward H. Gibbs, of NASA's Lewis Research Center in Cleveland, tested a rocket turbine question in this study. Turbopump drive turbines power the pumps that feed rocket engines. Their bearings need cooling, and coolant leaking into the flow could change how the turbine performs.

The team ran experiments at Lewis on a scale model turbine. They fed measured amounts of extra air ahead of the first rotor to simulate bearing coolant. At design speed and pressure ratio, added secondary flow lowered the turbine's work output and efficiency. Each added increment also raised the pressures between stages, most sharply at the nozzle exit.
podcast-joerogan-caK7O-T6rJE:
Writer Sebastian Junger tells Rogan, in a segment of the Joe Rogan Experience, about his brush with death. Junger, author of Tribe and The Perfect Storm, suffered a sudden internal bleed at home and nearly died before help arrived. He later wrote about what he saw as he faded.

He describes the presence he felt beside him, which he, an unbeliever, could not explain away. Rogan asks what the hour changed in his thinking about death and his father's ghost. The segment is a war reporter's most personal story, told with the same plain care he gave to soldiers' tales.
podcast-joerogan-eEOXc9ufQjE:
Rick Doblin talks MDMA with Rogan in a segment of the Joe Rogan Experience, busting myths and detailing breakthroughs. Doblin founded MAPS to turn MDMA into a legal therapy for trauma. By this visit, his trials had reached their final, decisive stage.

He separates the drug's real risks from the scare stories of the drug-war years, and lays out what the trial data showed for PTSD patients. Rogan asks what legal treatment would look like in practice. The segment is an advocate's update at a hopeful moment, careful with the facts because the finish line was finally in sight.
